description: A content-type definition, stored as an artifact. This is how a type becomes a first-class, collection-scoped, runtime-resolved object: a server self-registers each type it owns by writing one of these into a collection (the platform Types directory for first-party personas, or an app's own data collection for third-party apps). The platform resolves a type by reading the type-definition artifacts visible in the request's scope — never by scanning a server's filesystem. `context.target_content_type` is the type this artifact defines; `context.definition` is that type's full `type.json` (ui, operations, schema, the server-owned `ui.resource_uri` viewer pointer).

target_content_type.description: The content type this artifact defines (e.g. application/vnd.agience.chat+json).

definition.description: The full type.json the owning server published for target_content_type.

source.description: Provenance label for the publishing server (e.g. chorus/iris).
